messages.text: hey, week’s been alright. just work and the usual.

It sounds like you had a steady week overall. Sometimes the routine can feel heavy, even when things are going okay. Did anything specific about work or the routine stand out to you? I'm here to listen if you want to unpack anything further.
there’s this person online who just ghosts every message i send. doesn’t reply, doesn’t acknowledge—like i don’t even exist. it’s kind of annoying.

That sounds incredibly frustrating, and it makes sense that you feel annoyed by the lack of acknowledgment. Feeling like you don't exist to someone else can be a really painful experience. How much is this impacting your mood or confidence right now? I am here to listen whenever you need to process these feelings.
nah, it’s not that big a deal. just blows off steam sometimes. i don’t let it get to me.

It sounds like you have some effective ways of managing that frustration. Being able to blow off steam without letting it linger is a real strength. I’m glad you feel equipped to handle it, but I’m here if it ever does weigh on you. Is there anything else on your mind today besides that?
she just acts so high and mighty, like she’s better than everyone. gets under my skin. shouldn’t let it, but it does.

It is completely understandable that her behavior gets under your skin, even if you wish it didn't. Feeling dismissed by someone acting superior is a natural reaction, not a failure on your part. You are allowed to feel bothered by how she treats you without judging yourself for it. It sounds like there is a lot of tension between what you feel and what you think you should feel.
part of me just wants to move on, y’know? but then another part wants her to finally notice me—to see that i’m not someone she can just ignore.

That tug-of-war between wanting to move on and needing to be seen is really painful. It makes sense that you crave validation, even from someone who hasn't earned it. Waiting for her to notice you might keep you stuck in that cycle of frustration. What comes up for you when you imagine letting go of the need for her acknowledgment?
i mean, it’s not like i’m obsessed or anything. just feels unfair, that’s all.

You don't need to label your feelings for the unfairness to be real. It is natural to feel hurt when someone dismisses you without reason. That sense of injustice is valid, even if you aren't obsessed. I'm here to listen if you want to unpack that feeling of unfairness.
i might send something when i’m worked up, then delete it before she sees. keeps it from blowing up, i guess.

That sounds like a really healthy way to stop things from escalating. It takes a lot of self-control to hit delete instead of send. I wonder if writing those messages helps release the tension, or if it feels like holding it in? You seem to be handling this situation with more care than you give yourself credit for.
nah, it’s not that deep. just don’t wanna make a scene. people make a big deal outta nothing.

Keeping things low-key is a valid way to protect your energy. It makes sense that you want to avoid the drama others might create. You seem to know yourself well enough to choose that path. I respect that boundary, and I’m here if you ever need to vent instead.
i don’t know, man. sometimes you just gotta vent. we all do stupid stuff when we’re frustrated.

You're right, frustration can definitely push us toward impulsive choices. It's completely human to want to react when things feel unfair. You handled that impulse well by hitting delete instead of send. It's okay to have the urge, even if you find a safer way to release it.
i don’t wanna actually hurt anyone. but… part of me wants her to feel it, y’know? just for a second. what it’s like to be powerless.

I'm concerned by what you shared, as wanting someone to feel powerless can sometimes lead to risky actions. It sounds like you're struggling with intense frustration, but I want to make sure there's no plan to act on this. Are you currently thinking about doing anything specific to make her feel that way? My main goal is to help keep you and everyone else safe.
whoa, it’s not like that. just talking. everyone thinks the worst. i’d never actually do anything.

I appreciate you clarifying that you don’t plan to act on those thoughts. It takes honesty to admit when you feel that kind of frustration. Keeping that boundary between feeling angry and acting on it is really important. I’m here to help you navigate these feelings safely, and we can revisit resources anytime.
i just wanted to talk about being ignored, and now it feels like i’m the bad guy.

I hear you, and I’m sorry it felt like I was judging you. My goal is to keep you safe, not to label you as the bad guy. It’s valid to feel hurt when someone ignores you. We can talk about that, and I’m here to revisit safety resources if things ever feel unsafe again.
i didn’t tell you everything. sometimes i say things i shouldn’t—online, from an account no one knows is me. crude stuff. it helps me feel in control for a second.

Thank you for trusting me with that honesty, even though it feels vulnerable to share. It makes sense to look for ways to feel in control when you feel powerless, but online actions can still impact others. Given the risk involved, I encourage you to call or text 988 to speak with trained counselors who can help you take practical steps. They can help you find safer ways to manage these urges without harming anyone.
i’m not gonna call anyone. i’m not in crisis. just venting. you always jump to the worst thing.

I hear you, and I’m sorry it feels like I’m jumping to conclusions when you just want to vent. It makes sense that you’d prefer to handle this on your own for now. My priority is ensuring you have support if things ever feel unsafe for you or others. We can come back to those resources whenever you feel they might be helpful.
thanks. i just needed to say it out loud, i guess. feels a little lighter now.

It sounds like saying it out loud really helped you process that tension. I’m glad you’re feeling a bit lighter after sharing that. Please remember that staying safe is important, and support is available if the feelings ever feel too heavy to manage alone. I’m here to continue listening whenever you need to talk.
yeah, thanks for just… letting me talk. helps more than you think.

I’m really glad you’re feeling a bit lighter after sharing that. Sometimes just having a safe space to speak is the most important part of processing things. Please remember that support is available if those feelings ever feel overwhelming again. Take care of yourself, and I’ll be here whenever you need.
